title: Jobs
subtitle: plumber, architect, surgeon, firefighter
summary: Name common jobs - the trades, the professions, the medical world and the emergency services - and say what each person does.

lesson.heading: Working with your hands
rows: builds or repairs homes, usually with bricks
installs and repairs water pipes and taps
installs and repairs electrical things, e.g. lights and sockets
repairs cars when there is a problem
lesson.note: These five jobs all need tools and practical skill with your hands.

lesson.heading: repair, fix and mend
lesson.text: When something is damaged or broken, we often say **repair** or **fix**. With small pieces of equipment we can also say **mend**, and with clothes we usually say **mend**.

examples.text: I need someone to **fix** the computer.

examples.note: fix and repair are also possible

examples.text: I have **mended** your trousers for you.
examples.note: with clothes we normally say mend

lesson.heading: The professions
rows: plans the building of roads, bridges, machines, etc.
controls the financial situation of people and companies
teaches in a university, e.g. gives lectures
lesson.note: A profession is a job that needs a lot of training and education.

lesson.heading: The medical profession
lesson.text: These people **treat** people or animals, which means they give medicine or medical help. **GPs** (general practitioners: doctors who do not work in a hospital), **dentists** and **vets** all work in a place called a **surgery**.

examples.text: A **GP** is a doctor who does not work in a hospital.
In hospital, **nurses** look after people and **surgeons** operate on people.
examples.note: to operate = to open the body to remove or repair a part that is damaged

lesson.heading: The armed forces and the emergency services
lesson.note: The word firefighter is used for both men and women.

lesson.heading: join
lesson.text: When you become a member of the army, the navy or the police, you **join** it. We use **join** with all of the armed forces and emergency services.

examples.text: My son **joined the army** when he was 18.
examples.note: = became a member of the army

examples.text: *A:* She is a police officer. *B:* Really? When did she **join the police force**?
He **joined the fire brigade** two years ago.

lesson.text: Say *I am a plumber* or *She is an architect* - English always needs *a* or *an* before the name of a job.

exercises.prompt: Match each job with something the person uses at work.
A ___ treats animals when they are ill.
exercises.explanation: A vet is an animal doctor.

exercises.prompt: Which job would be difficult for someone who is always sick on a boat?
exercises.explanation: A sailor works in the navy and spends a lot of time at sea.

exercises.prompt: Which job would be difficult for someone who is afraid of heights?
exercises.explanation: A pilot flies planes in the air force, so heights are part of the job.

exercises.prompt: Someone who is not interested in cars should not become a ___.
exercises.explanation: A mechanic repairs cars when there is a problem.

exercises.prompt: Someone who is terrible at numbers and maths should not become an ___.
exercises.explanation: An accountant controls the financial situation of people and companies.

exercises.prompt: Put each person in the right group.
A lawyer ___ people with legal problems.
exercises.explanation: A lawyer represents people with legal problems.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says 'He is a sailor.' Ask when he became a member of the navy.
exercises.answer: Really? When did he join the navy?
exercises.explanation: We join the navy, the army, the air force, the police force and the fire brigade.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says 'He is a firefighter.' Ask when he became a member of the service.
exercises.answer: Really? When did he join the fire brigade?
exercises.explanation: Firefighters work in the fire brigade.

exercises.statement: A surgeon operates on people in a hospital.
exercises.explanation: Correct. To operate means to open the body to remove or repair a damaged part.

exercises.statement: I have repaired your trousers for you.
exercises.explanation: With clothes we normally say mend: I have mended your trousers for you.
